info.title: Granite Manager API
info.description: JSON API behind Granite Manager, a CRM for countertop and stone fabrication companies. Every request acts as the signed-in user and only sees data of that user's company.

get.description:
Returns the user behind the session, including their permission flags and
the company every other request acts in.

The user's details in their home company, and what the page shows: the
texting providers, the signature, and the guided tours rating.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or of the shop

put.description:
Saves the user's details in their home company. A new password ends the
user's other sessions and signs out their Granite Phone apps. The texting line is checked with its provider (the
`RingCentral` extension is looked up from the number), and a number moved
from `CloudTalk` to `RingCentral` brings its texting history along. A newly
filled email name or signature completes its setup task, with its points.

400.description: A field is invalid

403.description: Caller is not an employee or of the shop

409.description: The email belongs to another account

put.summary: Turn the recording voice of my calls on or off
put.description:
My Account > Phone lines > Granite Manager. Off: the user's outgoing
Granite Phone calls, Call via my cell calls and the Record button record
without saying "This call is being recorded." (some states require
telling the other side). Incoming calls keep their notice. 403 when the
home company does not call through Granite Phone.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or of the shop, or the company has no Granite Phone

400.description: The company has no RingCentral connection, or connect is not set up

403.description: Caller is not an employee

post.description:
Trades the code for the caller's own tokens, after checking they signed
in to the company's `RingCentral` account. Their line becomes the
extension that signed in and its texting number, their earlier texts
follow them, and `RingCentral` pushes their new texts to the CRM (a
failed subscription does not undo the connect).

400.description: Cancelled, expired or foreign state, another RingCentral account, or RingCentral refused the code

403.description: Caller is not an employee

delete.description:
Forgets the caller's own `RingCentral` sign-in; their line stays, but
texts from the CRM can't go out as them until they connect again.

403.description: Caller is not an employee

get.description:
Returns the position ids (job roles such as sales rep) the user holds in
the company the request acts in.

200.description: Position ids in the current company

get.description:
Returns the amount the signed-in user aims to sell each month, or null
when they have not set one. Set it with `PUT /v1/me/sales-goal`.

200.description: The goal, null when not set

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

put.description:
Saves the amount the signed-in user aims to sell each month (USD, above 0,
rounded to cents) and returns it as saved.

400.description: The amount is not above 0 or too large

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Returns whether the signed-in user's Telegram is linked to the lead alerts
bot and to the notifications bot, and the bots' ids for the Telegram login
widget. When a bot is configured, the saved link is checked with Telegram
first; a link Telegram rejects (bot blocked, chat gone) is removed and
reported as not linked, so the user is asked to connect again.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or of the shop

post.summary: Link my Telegram to the lead alerts bot
post.description:
Checks the Telegram login widget's signature (made in the last day) and
saves the Telegram id for lead alerts.

400.description: Bad, expired or forged login

401.description: No valid session, or another user's login

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

500.description: Bot not configured, or database error

post.summary: Link my Telegram to the notifications bot
post.description:
Like the lead alerts link, for the CRM notifications bot; shop staff may
link it too.

400.description: Bad, expired or forged login

401.description: No valid session, or another user's login

403.description: Caller is not an employee or shop staff

500.description: Bot not configured, or database error

put.description: Saves whether the desktop sidebar stays open (`pined_bar` on `GET /v1/me`).

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

put.summary: Turn my AI personal assistant on or off
put.description:
For users who have the AI personal assistant (`users.ai_promises` 1 = on,
2 = switched off by the user): off stops reading their calls, texts and
emails, the reminders and the morning list, and hides it in the CRM; on
resumes it. Users without it get 403.

403.description: Caller is not an employee, or has no AI personal assistant

post.description: Saves the signed-in user's rating of the guided tours; once per user.

400.description: Rating not 1-5 or text too long

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description: Which alerts the notifications Telegram bot sends the signed-in user.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

put.description: Turns each kind of Telegram alert on or off; returns the saved settings.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.summary: List the companies I market for
get.description:
Live companies where the signed-in user holds the External Marketing
position, for the marketing portal's company switcher.
The caller's to-dos, open ones first unless reordered by hand.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

post.description: It goes to the top of the list.

400.description: Empty or too long

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

put.description: Only the caller's own to-dos.

400.description: Empty or too long

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: Not the caller's to-do

delete.description: Someone else's to-do is left alone.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

put.description:
A ticked to-do moves to the bottom; an unticked one goes back above the
ticked ones.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: Not the caller's to-do

delete.description: Clears every to-do the caller ticked off.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

put.description: The caller's to-dos in the order given (others keep their place).

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Returns every non-deleted customer of the caller's company, optionally
filtered by sales rep. Invalid leads are hidden unless `show_invalid=1`.
With `view=companies` it returns only customers that have a company name,
each with revenue and project totals. Rows carry the primary email only;
use `POST /v1/customers/emails/batch` for all addresses.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
`customers` (default) lists every customer. `companies` lists only
customers with a company name and adds revenue and project totals.
Any other value is treated as `customers`.

parameters.name: sales_rep
parameters.description:
Only customers assigned to this sales rep (a user id, see
`GET /v1/users/sales-reps`). Omit or leave empty for all reps.

parameters.name: show_invalid
parameters.description:
`1` also returns leads marked invalid. Ignored when `view=companies`,
which never filters invalid leads out.

200.description: Customer rows, or company rows when `view=companies`

400.description: `sales_rep` is not an integer

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

post.description:
Saves a customer with its addresses (a phone or address of another
customer is refused). Without a sales rep, a sales rep creating a customer (other
than a walk-in) becomes its rep. An assigned customer gets an open deal
and an audit line; the telephony address books are updated.

400.description: Missing name, unknown source or sales rep

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

409.description: A phone or address belongs to another customer

get.summary: One page of the company's customers
get.description:
The customers page's table, filtered, sorted and paged here instead of
in the browser. Filters as `GET /v1/customers`, plus the tab's lead
sources; the onboarding sample customer is left out. Each page carries
every email of its customers, and `month_rows` the rows behind the
"this month" counts per sales rep.

parameters.name: tab
parameters.description:
`walkin` (default), `leads`, `call-in`, `other` (with `user-input`) or
`all`. Any other value matches no customers.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Sort column: `name`, `phone`, `email`, `sales_rep_name`,
`company_name`, `created_date`, `assigned_date`, and in the companies
view `revenue_generated`, `projects_count`. Omitted or unknown: newest
first by the tab's date (leads by when they were assigned).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page, default 1. Past the last page, the last page is returned.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page, default 20, at most 500.

400.description: `sales_rep` is not an integer

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

post.summary: Get all emails of several customers
post.description:
Returns every email address of the given customers, primary address
first, keyed by customer id. Customers without emails, and ids belonging
to another company, are absent from the result.

200.description: Map of customer id to email addresses, primary first

400.description: More than 20000 ids, or a malformed body

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Returns up to 15 live customers matching `term` by name (typos
tolerated, also matches the company name), phone digits, any email, or
company name. Customers with a live deal of the caller come first, then
the caller's own customers, then the best text matches. Each row carries
every email and the customer's latest deal. Fetch one in full with
`GET /v1/customers/{id}`.

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: What the user typed. Required (may be empty for phone search).

parameters.name: own_only
parameters.description: `true` returns only customers assigned to the caller or unassigned.

400.description: Missing `term` or unknown `by`

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Up to 5 live customers of the company that already have one of the
phones (last 10 digits) or addresses, for the "already exists" warning
of the add form. Empty without any contact.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email addresses (repeat the parameter), compared case-insensitively.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Addresses of the company's live customers matching `term` by name,
company or address, tolerating one typo in the address; with a domain
typed, every address of that domain. Best matches first, at most 15.
With `include_users`, also the company's users (empty `term`: all).

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: What was typed (name, company or address).

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Returns a customer of the caller's company with contact details, every
email address (primary first), the assigned sales rep and the lead form
answers. 404 for other companies' customers, and for deleted ones unless
`include_deleted=true` (a deal page still shows its deleted customer).

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Also return the customer when it was deleted.

400.description: Malformed query

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the caller's company

put.description:
Saves the contact details, source and addresses (exactly `emails`, the
first one primary). A new sales rep is recorded in the audit trail (with
the sales manager's original assignment of a lead first), stamps the
first assignment date, and gets the open deal.

400.description: Missing name, unknown source or sales rep

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such live customer in the company

409.description: A phone or address belongs to another customer

delete.description:
Hides the customer (soft delete) and removes it from the telephony
address books. A customer with live deals needs `cascade_deals=true`,
which hides the deals too. Admins and sales managers only.

parameters.name: cascade_deals
parameters.description: Also delete the customer's live deals (required when it has any).

403.description: Caller is neither an admin nor a sales manager

404.description: No such live customer in the company

409.description: The customer has live deals and `cascade_deals` is not set

put.description:
Records the change in the audit trail, stamps the first assignment
date, gives the rep the open deal and two reminders (text within a
day, check within three).

400.description: Unknown sales rep

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such live customer in the company

put.description: `hot`, `medium` or `cold`, or null to clear it.

400.description: Unknown temperature

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such live customer in the company

put.description:
Records why the lead is invalid, unassigns it and hides its live deals
(each deletion audited). Admins and sales managers only.

400.description: Missing reason

403.description: Caller is neither an admin nor a sales manager

404.description: No such live customer in the company

get.description:
The customer dialog's history: creation and assignment, deals (live,
created, deleted, won or lost), reassignments, email history (first
recording drips that were sent but are missing from it) and the
activities and notes of the live deals. Deleted customers included.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the company

get.description:
Documents sent to the customer for e-signature, newest first. Open
`SignWell` requests are checked with `SignWell` first.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the caller's company

post.description:
Answers a question from the customer's emails, texts, deal notes and
activities (and, with `include_calls`, transcripts of their last two
recorded calls), with links to the sources.

400.description: Question too short or too long

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the caller's company

get.description:
Reads the customer's last 30 texts and emails with AI and returns the
in-home estimate time both sides agreed on, if there is an exact one.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: The user's IANA time zone; the answer is on its clock.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the caller's company

get.description:
The live customers of the family the customer belongs to (its parent and
the parent's projects, or the customer and its own projects), by name,
with their addresses, newest deal stage and sales.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the company

put.summary: Link a customer under a parent
put.description: Makes the customer a project of `parent_id` (both of the company).

400.description: A customer cannot be its own parent

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: Customer or parent not in the company

get.description: The company's sales to the customer, newest first, with the seller.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such customer in the company

get.description:
Customers whose name matches `term` (typos allowed) or whose phone
contains its digits, and suppliers by name or phone.

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: A name (typos allowed) or phone digits; at least two characters.

200.description: Matches (none for a term under two characters)

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

Saves the phone as the customer's phone, or as the second phone when the

so the conversation shows their name.

400.description: Not a phone number (`invalid_phone`)

post.description:
A new customer with just a name and the phone, for an unknown number in
the SMS inbox.

400.description: `invalid_phone` or `empty_name`

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.summary: Find who a phone belongs to
get.description:
The company's live customer whose phone or second phone is this number
(with or without the country code), for an incoming call.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

400.description: Empty or too long

403.description: Caller is not an admin

409.description: A source with that name exists

put.description:
A built-in source only changes its label; a custom one also changes its

400.description: Empty or too long

403.description: Caller is not an admin

404.description: No such source in the caller's company

409.description: A source with that name exists

delete.description: Hides a custom source from the dropdown; its customers keep it.

400.description: A built-in source

403.description: Caller is not an admin

404.description: No such source in the caller's company

get.description:
Whether the visitor already entered a code for it, else where a code
would go. Unknown pages are 404.

404.description: No such page

post.description:
Sends a one-time code (10 minutes) to the customer's email. An address
gets at most one code every 45 seconds and 5 an hour; a new code
replaces the previous one.

404.description: No such page

429.description: A code was just sent, or 5 this hour

502.description: The email could not be sent

post.description:
Unlocks the page for this browser for 7 days. A code takes 8 attempts at
most.

400.description: Wrong or expired code, or too many attempts

404.description: No such page

get.description:
Newest first, with the stone, sink and how far the work is. Needs a
verified visitor.

401.description: No code entered for this page

404.description: No such page

get.description:
The quotes the customer made with the online quote, newest first: each
with its drawing and each color's total (no price breakdown). Only for a
verified visitor.

401.description: No code entered for this page

404.description: No such page

404.description: No such page

Only an invoice of this customer's `QuickBooks` customer. Needs a

400.description: Invalid invoice id

get.description:
Whether a code was asked for on the company's account page
(`pendingAccountLoginChallenge`).

post.summary: Email a code to an account's address
post.description:
Sends a code when a customer of the company has that email. The answer
is the same either way, so it does not reveal who is a customer. Same
limits as `send_customer_view_code`.

204.description: Sent (if the address is a customer's)

400.description: Not an email

429.description: A code was just sent, or 5 this hour

502.description: The email could not be sent

post.description:
Verifies the code sent to the account's address (8 attempts at most);
answers the page it unlocks.

400.description: Wrong or expired code, or too many attempts

delete.description: So the visitor can sign in with another email.

get.description:
Returns the non-deleted users of the caller's company who hold the sales
rep position. Use their ids for the `sales_rep` filter of `GET /v1/customers`.

200.description: Sales reps of the current company

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
The non-deleted employees of the caller's company by name ("User {id}"
when blank), e.g. to hide a calendar from one of them.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
The last 90 days of what the company's users did: deal activities (added,
completed, deleted), notes, deal pictures and documents, deals made and
deleted, users and customers added, texts and emails (matched to customers
by phone and address), newest first; the sales reps; and, while the
leaderboard is on, everyone's calls, texts and points in the table's days.

parameters.name: calls_from
parameters.description: First day of the "Calls & SMS points" table (default: the 1st of this month, UTC).

parameters.name: calls_to
parameters.description: Last day of that table, inclusive (default: today, UTC).

400.description: The table's days end before they start

403.description: Caller is not an admin

get.description:
The `CloudTalk` and `RingCentral` calls of the given users of the caller's
company over the last 90 days, and their Granite Phone calls (placed or
answered by them, and unanswered calls of their direct lines; `source`
`telnyx_call`), newest first. Users without a `CloudTalk` agent or
`RingCentral` extension, and companies without either, have no
`CloudTalk` or `RingCentral` calls.

403.description: Caller is not an admin

get.description:
The live users of the caller's company (superusers: of `company_id`, or
of every company), which of them only a superuser may change, the
companies the caller may pick with their user counts and limits, and
whether the listed company has `CloudTalk` or `RingCentral`.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: Superusers: one company's users (default every company's).

403.description: Caller may not manage users

post.description:
Creates a user with their email and positions in the caller's company
(superusers: in `company_id`) and emails them an invite link (7 days) to
set their own name, phone and password; they cannot sign in before. The
email must be unused, even by a deleted user. When the email fails the
user is still added: share the returned link instead.

400.description: Invalid email, or positions that can't go together

403.description: Caller may not manage users

get.description:
The user with their positions, marketing and Super Admin companies, the
companies the caller may pick (non-superusers: the user's own and the
ones a superuser granted marketing for) and their company's telephony.

403.description: Caller may not manage users, or only a superuser may change this one

404.description: No such live user of the caller's company

put.description:
Saves the user's details and positions. Positions that stay keep their
rows (Telegram lead buttons point at them). Non-superusers keep the
user's company, Super Admin and check-in positions and Super Admin
companies as they are, and may only grant marketing for the user's own
company (or remove companies a superuser granted). Super Admins are
always admins. The `RingCentral` extension follows the number. A user
who is no longer an employee or admin of their company (or moved to
another one) is signed out of Granite Phone.

400.description: Missing or invalid field, or positions that can't go together

403.description: Caller may not manage users, or only a superuser may change this one

404.description: No such live user of the caller's company

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a live user of the caller's company (superusers: any) and
signs out their Granite Phone apps.

403.description: Caller may not manage users, or only a superuser may delete this one

404.description: No such live user of the caller's company

post.description:
Emails a user who has not set up their account a new invite link (7
days); older links stop working. When the email fails the link is still
answered, to share another way.

403.description: Caller may not manage users, or only a superuser may change this one

404.description: No such live user of the caller's company

409.description: They already set up their account

get.summary: List the company's stones with slab availability
get.description:
Returns the stones of the caller's company that are on display (admins may
add hidden ones with `include_hidden=true`), sorted by name, each with counts of its slabs in the yard (`slabs`). Sold out stones
(no available slab and not regular stock) are hidden unless
`include_sold_out=true`; hidden and deleted stones are never returned.
Filters combine with AND; list filters take the parameter repeated and
match any value. Color ids come from the colors list, supplier ids from
the suppliers list.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only stones of these types, e.g. `granite`, `quartz`, `marble`.

parameters.name: supplier_id
parameters.description: Only stones bought from this supplier (a supplier id).

parameters.name: color_id
parameters.description: Only stones tagged with at least one of these colors (color ids).

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Only stones of these price levels (1 = cheapest ... 7).

parameters.name: finishing
parameters.description: Only stones with these surface finishes: `polished`, `leathered`, `honed`.

parameters.name: include_sold_out
parameters.description:
`true` also returns sold out stones: no available slab and not regular
stock. Default `false`.

parameters.name: include_hidden
parameters.description:
`true` also returns stones hidden from the catalogs (`is_display`
false). Admins only (403 otherwise). Default `false`.

400.description: A filter has the wrong type, e.g. `supplier_id=abc`

403.description: Caller is not an employee or shop staff, or asks for hidden stones without being an admin

post.description:
Creates a stone of the caller's company with its image (an upload to the
`stones` folder, thumbnail made here) and colors. Add its slabs with
`POST /v1/stones/{id}/slabs`.

400.description: Missing name or image, unknown type, supplier or color, bad finishing, level, size or date

403.description: Caller is not an admin

503.description: Uploads are not configured

get.summary: Search the company's stones by name
get.description:
Returns up to `limit` stones whose name contains `name`, best matches
first (name starts with it, then contains it as a word), each with the
same fields and slab counts as `GET /v1/stones`. By default only
displayed stones that are regular stock or have an available whole slab;
see `include_sold_out` and `include_hidden`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part of the stone name, case-insensitive. Empty returns no stones.

parameters.name: include_sold_out
parameters.description:
`true` also returns sold out stones. By default a stone is listed
when it is regular stock or has an available whole slab.

parameters.name: include_hidden
parameters.description:
`true` also returns stones hidden from the catalog (`is_display`
false). Default `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most stones to return, 1 to 50. Default 25.

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type

403.description: Caller is not an employee, admin or of the shop

post.summary: Add a stone with its slabs in one step
post.description:
Creates a displayed stone and either one leftover slab (bundle
`LO-YYYYMMDD-XXXX`) or one slab per bundle label, all with the given
size. Used while selling a slab that is not in the system yet. Returns
the stone and the new slab ids, ready to put on a sale.

400.description: Missing name, non-positive price, negative size, unknown stone type, or no bundles

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

get.description:
Returns every field of a stone of the caller's company, including hidden
(not displayed) stones, plus the ids of its colors. Deleted stones and
stones of other companies are 404. List its slabs with
`GET /v1/stones/{id}/slabs`.

403.description: Caller is not an employee or admin

404.description: No such stone in the caller's company

put.description:
Saves every field of the body on a stone of the caller's company and
replaces its colors. With a new `image_url` the image is replaced and the
old file deleted; without one the image is kept.

400.description: Invalid field (see `create_stone`)

403.description: Caller is not an admin

404.description: No such stone in the caller's company

parameters.name: include_slabs
parameters.description:
`true` also hides the stone's slabs in the yard. Without it, a stone
that still has slabs is not deleted (409).

403.description: Caller is not an admin

404.description: No such stone in the caller's company

409.description: The stone has slabs and `include_slabs` is not set

get.description:
Returns the slabs and remnants in the yard for a stone: its own plus
those of the stones it draws from (linked stones, marked with
`source_stone`). Cut and deleted slabs are left out. Sold slabs carry
their sale (customer, seller, date, notes, room, sinks); remnants carry
the sale of the slab they were cut from. Ordered by slab id; group by
`bundle` for display. Sell an available slab with the sales routes,
resize one with `PATCH /v1/slabs/{id}`.

403.description: Caller is not an employee, admin or of the shop

404.description: No such stone in the caller's company

post.summary: Add a slab to a stone
post.description:
Adds a slab in the yard with a bundle label, a size (the stone's size
when length and width are 0 or missing) and an optional photo (an upload
to the `stones` folder).

400.description: Empty bundle, negative size, or a photo URL that is not an upload

403.description: Caller is not an admin

404.description: No such stone in the caller's company

patch.description:
Saves the samples on hand and/or how many to keep for a stone of the
caller's company.

400.description: Negative amount, importance not 1-4, or nothing to save

403.description: Caller is not an employee or shop staff

404.description: No such stone in the caller's company

post.description:
Texts (else emails) customers their 24-hour and 1-hour reminders, and
notifies reps the day before and an hour before. Reminders for
appointments that already started are marked failed.

At 9 AM store time, sends each shop worker and shop manager with Telegram
notifications a list of their company's equipment checks due today, once a
day, and pushes how many there are to the signed-in phones of each shop
worker and shop manager (Telegram linked or not).

Inside the send window, sends the survey invitations and reminders that
are due.

Pulls reps' outbound calls into the call points table, then transcribes
and classifies a few of the calls long enough to need it.

Saves the `CloudTalk` and `RingCentral` calls of every connected company,
so they stay in its history after it changes provider. Also renews reps'
own `RingCentral` sign-ins before they lapse unused.

Expires open requests past their expiry, then sends due reminders and
the senders' notifications. Called by the `time-triggered` Lambda with
`Authorization: <LAMBDA_KEY>`. While native signatures are not enabled
it does nothing.

Sends the due steps of SMS / email flows, the drip texts of lead lists
and everyone's scheduled emails and texts.

Returns files stuck in processing to the queue, then processes waiting
files (newest first) until none is left or ten minutes have passed.

Pushes a few customers without a `RingCentral` or `CloudTalk` contact to
their company's provider.

Signs out the phones of users who may no longer use Granite Phone (or
whose company was deleted) and browser phones whose CRM sign-in ended, deletes
leftover Telnyx credentials of signed-out phones (backing off on
failures), deletes Telnyx callbacks older than 30 days, closes calls
Telnyx never reported the end of (after 6 hours), keeps the customer
phone index that matches calls to customers in step (customers changed
or added since the last run; each company's first fill, at most 5,000
customers a run), writes up to 3 AI notes (transcript, note tidied like
the CRM's, on the call and its deal, the deal's people notified), gives
answered outbound calls their call points (provider `telnyx`), deletes
Telnyx's copies of copied recordings whose delete failed, retries failed
recording copies (5 attempts), brings port-in orders up to date from
Telnyx (adding ported numbers to the company), and last reads sent 10DLC
texting registrations and pending number assignments again. Bounded work per run, and
no new work after 20 seconds; the next run takes the rest. Returns what
was done.

post.summary: Run one tick of the PostHog auto-fix intake
post.description:
Gives up on fix runs that never reported back, then (at most once per
poll window, `POSTHOG_AUTOFIX_POLL_MINUTES`) reads the PostHog
`$exception` events since the last read (never before the cutover) and
records them as bugs, one per signature whatever issue they are in;
judges bugs that have settled (skipped as noise, a browser 5xx folded into
the API error of the same route, a toast folded into the web error it
repeats, or queued); emails when a fixed issue is reopened; and (with
`POSTHOG_AUTOFIX_WRITE_KEY` and `_ASSIGNEE` set) assigns the issues of
opened fixes in PostHog. Last, in live mode, it starts queued fix runs
(bugs seen in the last day first, then the most widespread) within the
concurrency and daily caps; in dry-run mode it emails the runs it would
have started instead. With `POSTHOG_AUTOFIX_MODE` off it does nothing.
When another tick is running it returns at once with `busy`. PostHog or
GitHub failures do not fail the call: they are listed in `errors` and
retried on the next tick.

post.summary: Run the AI check of a texting registration (10DLC)
post.description:
Takes the registration that has waited longest for its AI check (or one
whose check stopped midway, after 15 minutes), reads its quote form,
privacy policy, terms and website, and has the AI check them and the
form the way the carriers do. The Manager who marked it ready is
emailed what to change, or that it passed; one that passed is ready and
the superusers are told (bell and email). After 3 runs where the AI
could not answer it goes to the superusers unchecked.

post.summary: Read reps' calls and messages for promises
post.description:

due, closes the tasks they finished in the CRM (a quote saved or emailed,
a document sent to sign, an event on the schedule, a call), sends their
morning list (once a day from 8 AM their time), queues their calls, texts
and emails of the last 3 days not read yet, then reads up to 4 (a call is
transcribed first): saves what the rep promised the customer and by when,
closes the open promises it keeps, adds the quote work the customer gave
them to that customer's one quote task, and writes the text or email that
keeps each promise a message can keep, in the rep's own style.

Called once by the `posthog-autofix` GitHub workflow when it begins,
before the agent runs. Moves the run from `dispatched` to `running` and
stores the GitHub run link. `issue_id` must be the run's PostHog issue id.
Repeating the same call (same `github_run_url`) answers 200 with
`changed: false`. Any other status (for example a run the intake never
dispatched) answers 409, and the workflow must stop. Uses the callback
secret, not a session.

parameters.name: id

Called once by the `posthog-autofix` GitHub workflow when it ends. Closes
the run as `succeeded` (`conclusion` completed, with the agent's answer in
`agent`) or `failed`, stores the outcome, pull request, verification and
cost, and emails the developers. A `usage_limited` conclusion puts the run
back in the queue to be retried in an hour, with no email, until its
attempts run out; then it fails. A late result for a run the watchdog
timed out is still recorded. Repeating a result answers 200 with
`changed: false` and sends no second email. A result for a run that never
started answers 409. Uses the callback secret, not a session.

post.description:
Signs the Granite Phone app in with the CRM email and password and
returns its device token (send it as the `X-Granite-Device` header) and
its call key (signs the calls it places), both shown only here. Only
employees, admins and superusers of a company that is not deleted may:
others get 403 `no_phone_access`.
Failed attempts count together with `POST /v1/auth/login`'s (10 per
email and address, 50 per email in 15 minutes, then 429
`rate_limited`), and a wrong email and a wrong password both answer 401
`invalid_credentials`. The sign-in lasts until the phone signs out or is
revoked, never ending by time. Next:
`POST /v1/phone/devices` registers the phone for calling.

201.description: Signed in; the device token and call key are in the body

400.description: A field is missing or empty, or the platform is unknown

403.description: `no_phone_access`: not an employee, admin or superuser, or the company is deleted

429.description: `rate_limited`: too many failed attempts; try later

delete.description:
Ends the device session of the request's `X-Granite-Device` token: the
token stops working, the phone's Telnyx credential is deleted and its
push token cleared. The app then wipes its local data. Device token only.

get.description:
The caller's Granite Phone sign-ins that are not signed out, newest
first; `current` marks the phone making the request (always false with
the CRM's cookie). Revoke one with `DELETE /v1/me/devices/{id}`. Takes
the device token or the session cookie (employees, admins, superusers).

401.description: No valid device token or session

403.description: Cookie of a user who is not an employee or admin

delete.summary: Sign one of my phones out
delete.description:
Revokes one of the caller's device sessions (an id from
`GET /v1/me/devices`; it may be the calling phone itself): its token stops
working, its Telnyx credential is deleted and the phone is told to wipe
itself. 404 when the session is not the caller's or is signed out already.
Takes the device token or the session cookie.

401.description: No valid device token or session

403.description: Cookie of a user who is not an employee or admin

404.description: Not one of the caller's signed-in phones

get.description:
One call at app start, on resume after 5 minutes and after a push wake:
the user, this phone's registration, caller IDs, settings, availability,
the company's switches (calling, recording mode, minimum app version),
the notices to show, the contact index's version and the unread counts.
Device token only. Next: `POST /v1/phone/devices` when `device` is null,
`GET /v1/phone/contacts/index` when `contacts.etag` changed.

post.description:
Registers the phone of this device session for calling, or updates it
(idempotent: 201 the first time, 200 after). While calling is on for the
company it also gets its Telnyx telephony credential (working 30 days,
extended with every login JWT); `sipUsername` stays null while calling is
off. A `pushToken` here or later (`PUT .../push-token`) lets us push
missed calls; no other phone keeps that token. Device token only. Next:
`POST /v1/phone/devices/{id}/token`.

400.description: Missing device name, unknown platform or too long a push token

502.description: Telnyx did not create the credential; try again

post.description:
Mints a Telnyx login JWT (about 24 hours) for this phone's SIP credential
and extends the credential to 30 days; makes the credential first when
the phone has none yet. At most one a minute and six an hour per phone
(429 with `retryAfterSecs`); a failed mint does not count. 403
`calling_disabled` while the company's calling is off, 403
`update_required` when the app is older than the minimum version (the
version in `X-Granite-App-Version` when sent, which is also saved; else
the registered one), 404 when `id` is not this session's phone. The
native calling module calls it too, with the same headers.

403.description: `calling_disabled` or `update_required`

404.description: Not this session's phone

429.description: `rate_limited`: one a minute, six an hour

503.description: Telnyx is not set up on the server

put.description:
Saves the phone's FCM registration token (after it changes), for our
pushes: missed calls, voicemails, AI messages, new emails, sign-outs. No
other phone keeps the token. 404 when `id` is not this session's phone. The native
calling module calls it too.

400.description: Empty or too long

404.description: Not this session's phone

get.description:
The company numbers the user may call from (direct lines first, then
shared lines, then the main line) and the one to preselect. Device token
only.

put.description:
Changes only the fields sent: default caller ID, AI notes, working
hours, cell fallback, ring timeout, "Forward all calls", incoming call
information (display number, announcements, answer PIN) and hold music;
returns all the settings. The cell number changes only through
`POST /v1/phone/cell/verify` and `/confirm`; Do not disturb through
`PUT /v1/phone/availability`; custom rules through
`/v1/phone/call-rules`. 400 `not_a_caller_id`, `cell_not_verified`,
`invalid_phone`, `invalid_pin`, `pin_required`, `invalid_hold_music`, or
a message for bad hours or timeouts. Device token only.

400.description: `not_a_caller_id`, `cell_not_verified`, `invalid_phone`, `invalid_pin`, `pin_required`, `invalid_hold_music`, or what is wrong

put.description:
`available` ends Do not disturb; `dnd` turns it on until `dndUntil`, or
until turned off when that is null. Returns the availability now, which
is `outside_hours` when the user is available but outside their working
hours. While not available, calls go to the number's fallback (and still
show in Recents). Device token only.

400.description: Unknown status, or `dndUntil` not in the next year

post.description:
Records that the user accepted this version of the recording notice or
the 911 notice (on this phone); accepting again is fine. 400 for a
version that does not exist (below 1 or above the current one). Device
token only.

400.description: Unknown notice or version

post.description:
Our server calls `cellNumber` (US or Canada) from a company number and
reads out a 6-digit code, valid 10 minutes; send it to
`POST /v1/phone/cell/confirm`. The verified cell stays as it is until the
new one is confirmed. At most one code call a minute and five a day
(429, also when the code was confirmed or voided since), and each takes
one of the user's 6 calls a minute (429 while those are used up); a
call Telnyx did not place does not count. 400 `invalid_phone`; 403
`calling_disabled` while the company's calling is off or it has no
number to call from. Takes the device token or the session cookie (the
CRM's phone dock verifies the cell for Call via my cell).

400.description: `invalid_phone`

401.description: No valid device token or session

403.description: `calling_disabled`, or a cookie of a user who is not an employee or admin

429.description: `rate_limited`: a code call went out less than a minute ago, five today, or 6 calls this minute

502.description: Telnyx did not place the call; try again

503.description: Telnyx is not set up on the server

Checks the code our call read out; when right, the pending number
becomes the verified cell (`cellNumber` in the settings returned). 400
`wrong_code` for a wrong, expired or used-up code (5 tries, then ask for
a new call). Takes the device token or the session cookie.

400.description: `wrong_code`

403.description: A cookie of a user who is not an employee or admin

get.description:
The compact index of the company's customers (all live ones but the
onboarding sample) and coworkers, for search on the phone. Without

follow `nextAfter` with `?after=`). With `?since=<cursor>`: the customers
changed, added or called since, and the ids deleted since (a full
download when the cursor is too old or there are more than 5,000
changes). Deal changes (open deal, stage) reach the phone with a full
download, which the app does daily, so a full download always answers
the index. `If-None-Match` with the ETag of the last answer (or
`GET /v1/phone/bootstrap` `contacts.etag`) answers 304 when nothing
changed, on a since-sync only. Later pages (`after`) carry no `ETag`.
Device token only.

unreadable cursor gets a full download instead).

parameters.description: The ETag of the phone's copy: 304 when the index is unchanged (since-syncs only)

A customer of the company with their email, rep and address, their live

call of a direct line assigned to them, and unanswered incoming calls of

answered, voicemails and AI messages included), `incoming`,
`outgoing` or `recorded` (with a recording).

The caller's answered calls (placed or taken) and their talk time today,
this week (from Monday) and this month, in the company's time zone (its
business hours' zone, else America/Indiana/Indianapolis). Device token
only.

A link to the call's recording that works 5 minutes. Only for those who
may hear the call (403 for others): its user, the users of the direct
line it came in on or went out from, for an incoming call nobody
answered the users its line rings, the owner of its deal, company admins
and sales managers. 404 when the call has no recording (or is another
company's). Device token only.

Adds a deal note (by the caller) on the call's deal, or else on the
oldest open deal of the call's customer, and tells the deal's people
like a note written in the CRM. 400 `no_deal` when the call has neither;

"Call via my cell" (no data on the phone, or from the CRM): our server
rings the caller's verified cell from the caller ID; they press 1 and
the customer is dialed, recorded and logged (`viaCell` in Recents). The
customer is the one sent when it is the company's, else the number's.
400 `invalid_phone` (callable US and Canada numbers only), `no_cell`
(no verified cell), `not_a_caller_id`; 403 `calling_disabled`; 429
`rate_limited` (6 calls a minute, and the company's daily limit; counted
for all the user's phones and the CRM together). Takes the device token
or the session cookie.

The call health check: our server calls this phone (its SIP user) from
the caller's default caller ID (else a company number) and plays a short
message. Test calls are not in Recents or stats; follow it with
`GET /v1/phone/calls/{id}`. 400 when the phone is not registered; 403
`calling_disabled`; 429 `rate_limited` (6 calls a minute). Device token
only.

403.description: `calling_disabled`

502.description: Telnyx did not place the call; try again

503.description: Telnyx is not set up on the server

post.description:
Best effort, after the user declined on this phone: the call's leg to
this phone is marked declined, and when the call still rings, nobody
answered and no other person's phone rings, the caller goes on to the
number's no-answer action (AI Assistant, voicemail or forward), which
stops the user's other phones. On a shared line that also rings others,
only this phone stops. Unknown ids are ignored. Device token only.

400.description: Empty id

post.description:
The app opened the phone's own dialer for an emergency or N11 code (the
call never goes through Telnyx); this tells the company's admins at once:
an in-app notification for each, and an `e911_alert` push to their
phones signed in to the company. The caller is not alerted. Alerts are
deduplicated for 10 minutes per phone: a repeat of the same code, or
any code after an emergency code (911, 112, 933, 988), alerts nobody
again (still 204); an emergency code after another N11 code does. 400
`invalid_phone` for anything but an N11 or emergency code. Device token
only.

400.description: `invalid_phone`: not an emergency or N11 code

post.description:
"Report a problem" from the app's settings: emails support the user's
summary, the app version, the phone model and the app's recent log,
with phone numbers masked (to their last 4 digits) and tokens removed;
replies go to the user. Long reports are cut (2,000 characters of
summary, 500 log lines). At most 3 reports an hour per phone (429 with
`retryAfterSecs`); a report that could not be sent does not count.
Device token only.

The conversations of the numbers I may call from, one per line and other
number, newest activity first (page back with `before` = `nextBefore`),
optionally only those with one other `number`, or only those with texts I
haven't read (`unread=true`, paged the same way). Each has our line, the
other number, the customer with it, the newest text and my unread count;
`unread` totals every thread. 403 `texting_disabled` unless the company
texts through Telnyx. Next: `GET /v1/phone/texts/threads/{key}/messages`.

parameters.description: Only the threads with this other number (E.164 or 10 digits).

parameters.description:
`true`: only the threads with texts I haven't read (the Unread tab).
Default `false`, every thread.

The newest texts of one of my threads (newest first; page back with
`before` = `nextBefore`), each with its pictures and files (links from
`GET /v1/phone/texts/media/{id}`), status, error and sender, and the
thread itself. 404 for a thread that is not one of my lines' (or has no
texts). Opening it does not mark it read: `POST .../read` does.

parameters.description: `nextBefore` of the previous page (a text id).

The thread a text is in (one of my lines and one other number), as
`GET /v1/phone/texts/threads` lists it: its `key`, the other number, the
customer, the newest text and my unread count. The app's new-text
notification starts here: the `text` push names only the text
(`textId`), never the number or the thread. 404 for a text that is not
on one of my lines (or another company's). Device token only.

for one that is not.

(US and Canada only) and returns it (`queued`; Telnyx's delivery events
update it), with the thread marked read for me. Files from
`POST /v1/sms/attachments` go with it (pictures as MMS, other files as
links). 400 `invalid_phone`, a bad text (up to 1600 characters, a text or
a file), or a bad file (`invalid_attachment`, `too_many_images`,
`images_disabled`), 403 `texting_disabled` /
`not_my_line`, 409 `opted_out` (the person texted STOP), 429
`rate_limited` (ten texts a minute, shared with the CRM) with
`retryAfterSecs`, 502 when Telnyx failed.

follow). 404 for a thread that is not one of my lines'.

get.description:
The company's Granite Phone numbers (main line first, then shared and
direct lines), who each one rings and who may call from it; the users
numbers can be given to (employees and admins, by name); and the
company's calling status (`enabled`, `recordingMode`, `configured` =
Telnyx is set up). Change a number with `PUT
/v1/phone/admin/numbers/{id}`; add the TeXML app's numbers with `POST
/v1/phone/admin/numbers/import`. Company admins (and super admins,

call nobody answers does (`ai`, `voicemail`, `forward` with `forwardTo`,
a US or Canada number), the voicemail greeting, whether it is active, and

Reads the numbers assigned to the company's TeXML app in Telnyx and adds
the ones that are missing here as unassigned direct lines (no label,
the AI Assistant when nobody answers); numbers already here are left as
they are. Returns how many were added and the company's numbers. 400
when Telnyx is not set up for the company (no TeXML app saved), 503
when Telnyx is not set up on the server, 502 when Telnyx fails. Company

get.description:
Every Granite Phone sign-in of the company's users that is not signed
out (expired and idle ones stay listed until revoked), newest first,
with whose phone it is and its Telnyx SIP user. Sign one out with
`DELETE /v1/phone/admin/devices/{id}`. Company admins (and super admins,

delete.description:
Revokes a device session of the company (an id from
`GET /v1/phone/admin/devices`): its token stops working at once, the
phone is told to wipe itself (a `revoked` push), its Telnyx credential

post.description:
The first send (Telnyx charges for the brand, and for the campaign
three months up front): registers the business as a brand, then, once

the phone job create it when the brand takes longer). Never a second

first. The form must be complete (the company's Managers usually mark it
ready first) and the company needs its Telnyx setup (Telnyx reports to
its webhooks). With an AI on the server, its check must have passed this
form within the last 24 hours (pages change): an older check, or none,
is asked for again and the send answers 409 until it passes (the
superusers are told, in minutes). Returns the review: `sent` while the
brand registers, `campaign_pending`, or `rejected` with Telnyx's reasons.

the brand (nothing was made); 409 when sent already (use `.../resend`),
another send runs, or the AI check has not passed this form within a
day; 502 when Telnyx did not answer about the brand; 503 when Telnyx is
not set up on the server. Audited. Superusers only.

Telnyx's TeXML app voice URL, fetched when someone calls one of the
company's numbers (`To`). First the company's spam and blocked numbers
(`GET /v1/phone/admin/call-blocking`): a trusted number is never
blocked; a hidden number (when the company blocks those), a blocked
number or area code, or likely spam (STIR/SHAKEN validation failed, or
Telnyx's call screening says `SPAM LIKELY`; when the company blocks spam
or sends it to voicemail) is logged as blocked and hears the
announcement then a hang-up, is rejected, or goes to voicemail without
ringing anyone; blocked calls get no missed-call push. Otherwise the
call is logged (`ringing`; the customer is the company's newest live
customer with the caller's number; `spamLikely` when the caller-ID check
says so) and answered with TeXML: "This call may be recorded." when the
company records incoming calls, then a `<Dial>` ringing every signed-in
phone of the users whose part of the call is to ring (not Do not
disturb, no forward of all calls, their first matching incoming call
rule, else their working hours; the main line only while the company is
open), with `dial-result` as its action, a `leg-status` callback per
phone, the `whisper` announcement for users who turned it on, and the
number called as the caller ID when every one of them chose to see it.
On a user's own direct line their forward, voicemail or message rule
takes the whole call (no missed-call push). When no phone can ring it
goes straight on: the cells of users with cell fallback on, else the
number's no-answer action (AI Assistant, voicemail or forward) and a
`missed_call` push. A repeated request answers the same call again. An
internal error answers the fallback TeXML (`<Redirect>`). 403 when the
number, account or connection is not the token's company's.

request had none). A final status (`completed`, `busy`, `no-answer`,
`canceled`, `failed`) ends the call once, at Telnyx's time: `answered`
with its talk time when someone answered; else an incoming call becomes
`canceled` (the caller hung up while it rang), `busy` or `failed`, and an
unfinished Call via my cell `canceled` or `failed`; a missed call keeps
its status (voicemail, AI message ...). Then the follow-through: a
missed-call push when the caller hung up while it rang, and for a
customer, the deal leaves its first stage after a talk of 90 seconds or
more and the customer's SMS flows stop. Other statuses and unknown calls
are only stored.

The `recordingStatusCallback` of a recorded `<Dial>` (`kind=call`) or a
voicemail's `<Record>` (`kind=voicemail`). When Telnyx says the recording
is `completed`, it is looked up by `RecordingSid` with our key (never
the callback's link) and must be of this call (Telnyx's call ids for it
include one of the call's, its connection is the company's; else
nothing is stored or deleted), downloaded, stored once in the private
recordings bucket at `phone/{company}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{call id}-{kind}.mp3`
and checked (our copy's size must match); then Telnyx's copy is deleted
(retried by the phone job when that fails). The call gets
`hasRecording`, and is queued for transcription (`transcriptStatus`
`pending`) when the call's user has AI notes on, for any voicemail, and
for an answered outgoing call (its transcript scores it; its AI note
still needs AI notes on). Each copy
counts as an attempt; one that fails leaves the recording pending for
the phone job to retry. Repeats and other statuses change nothing.

of a parked app call: approved (transferred to the number with the
user's caller ID, `command_id` `approve-{call id}`; recorded only after
a notice, see the module docs) or hung up and logged `failed`; see the
checks in the module docs. Emergency codes (911, 112, 933, 988) are
never refused (the admins get an `e911_alert`, at most one per phone in
10 minutes). Later events of the call update it: `call.answered` of the
customer's leg (answered, at Telnyx's time; a call recorded after the
spoken notice gets it, then its recording; `call.bridged` changes
nothing, the customer's phone may still ring),
`call.hangup` (final status, talk time, the CRM follow-through),
`call.recording.saved` (the recording is copied to the private bucket).
Every event is stored and handled once.

requestBody.description: A 10DLC event, as Telnyx sends it: `data.event_type` (`10dlc.brand.update`, `10dlc.campaign.update`, `10dlc.phone_number.update`), `data.id`, `data.occurred_at`, `data.payload` (`brandId` or `campaignId`, `type` such as `REGISTRATION`, `TELNYX_REVIEW`, `MNO_REVIEW`, `VERIFIED`, `ASSIGNMENT`, `STATUS_UPDATE`; `status`, `description`, `reasons[]` with `description` and `fields`, `phoneNumber`)

200.description: Taken (or not the company's, or seen before: nothing to do)

400.description: Not JSON

401.description: Telnyx's signature is missing or does not check out

404.description: No company has this webhook token

500.description: It could not be handled (database, or Telnyx unreachable): Telnyx sends it again

503.description: Telnyx signatures are not set up on the server (`TELNYX_PUBLIC_KEY`)

e.description: The email the link came from.

email_name.description: The name recipients see in the From field.

ringcentral_signed_in.description:
Texts from the CRM go out as the user through `RingCentral`: they
connected their own `RingCentral` (`/v1/me/ringcentral`), or theirs is
the login the company connected with.

shows_email_signature.description: The signature applies (not for shop managers and workers).

has_onboarding_feedback.description: The user already rated the guided tours.

feedback_dismissed.description: The user dismissed the tours rating.

has_granite_phone.description: The home company calls through Granite Phone (Telnyx calling is on).

granite_phone_numbers.description:
The Granite Phone numbers the user can call from (E.164); an admin
assigns them on the Phone page.

recording_voice.description:
The user's calls say "This call is being recorded." to both sides when
their recording starts (`PUT /v1/me/recording-voice`).

Body of `PUT /v1/me/account`. A field left out keeps its value; an empty
one clears it.

password.description: A new password (at least 8 characters); empty keeps the current one.

email_signature.description: The email signature (HTML, sanitized on save).

ringcentral_phone_number.description: `RingCentral` line (10+ digits); the extension is looked up from it.

texting_line_status.description:
The texting line: `saved`, `unchanged`, `unmatched` (the provider did
not confirm it), `incomplete` (a `CloudTalk` line without its agent id)
or `none` (no line submitted).

texting_line_provider.description: The provider of that line (`CloudTalk`, `RingCentral`); null for `none`.

oneOf.description: Setup tasks this save finished, with their points; null when none.
The priced lines get this product.
The priced lines never get this product (another one is learned).
Text lines with the phrase are left out (the editor offers them back).

A text line added at the end.
The invoice's class.
The invoice's CC.

company_id.description: A company the caller holds the Super Admin position in.

enrollment_id.description: The phone's enrollment in the flow.

next_step_position.description: Position of the next step (1 = first).

flows.description: The flows turned on, of every calendar, oldest first.

deal_id.description: Deal it belongs to.

deadline.description: Store wall time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` (midnight means a whole day), or null.

ActivityEvent.description: An event with its latest activity.

unscheduled.description: Waiting for its day (not on the calendar).

assignee_name.description: The installer or template maker on it.

lines.description: Its last three lines, oldest first.

name.description: What to do, at most 255 characters.

deadline.description:
`YYYY-MM-DD` (whole day), or a store wall time
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` / `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. A time sends the deal
owner a reminder then.

oneOf.description: Default `medium`.

ActivityLine.description: A change to an event or a comment on it.

sales_reps.description: The company's sales reps, by name.

call_sms_points.description:
Calls, texts and points per user in the table's days; null while the
company's leaderboard is off.

deadline.description: New deadline (same formats as when creating); null clears it.

oneOf.description: New priority.

ActivityPreview.description: An activity preview on a customer's deal.

ActivityRep.description: A sales rep of the company.

include_calls.description: Also transcribe the last two recorded calls (slower, costs more).

label.description: What it is and when.

href.description: Where to open it in the CRM (emails and texts).

uses.description: How many live activities the caller created with it.

urls.description: URLs of uploads to the `stones` folder (`POST /v1/uploads`), 1 to 50.

phone.description: The number to add: E.164 or 10 digits (US or Canada).

replacePhone2.description:
When phone and phone 2 are both used: replace phone 2 (else 409
`phone_2_taken`).

AddPhotos.description: Body of the add photos routes.

urls.description: URLs of uploads to the model's folder, 1 to 50.

deal_id.description: Deal to save the attachment on.

slab_id.description: A free slab of the company.

room_uuid.description: That room's id (hex), when it has one.

AdminDevice.description: A phone signed in to the company.

id.description: The device session: pass it to `DELETE /v1/phone/admin/devices/{id}`.

deviceName.description: The name the phone gave at sign-in.

platform.description: `android` or `ios` (the app), or `web` (a browser phone of the CRM).

appVersion.description:
The app version at sign-in; null when it sent none (always for a
browser phone).

lastSeenAt.description:
When it was last used (updated at most every 5 minutes); null when
never since sign-in.

current.description:
The caller's own phone: always false here (the admin page signs in
with the session cookie).

sipUsername.description:
The phone's SIP user on Telnyx (`gencred...`); null until it
registered for calling with calling on.

devices.description: The company's phones that are not signed out, newest first.

AdminNumber.description: A company number, as the admin page edits it.

label.description: Its label, e.g. "Main line"; may be empty.

kind.description:
`direct` (one person's line), `shared` (a team line) or `main` (the
company's main line, which rings only in business hours).

noAnswerAction.description:
What a call nobody answers does: `ai` (the AI Assistant), `voicemail`
or `forward` (to `forwardTo`).

forwardTo.description: Where `forward` sends calls, E.164; null when none.

greeting.description:
What callers hear before leaving a voicemail; null = the standard
greeting.

active.description: In use: an inactive number rings nobody and is nobody's caller ID.

assignments.description:
Who it rings and who may call from it, by user id (users of the
company only).

numbers.description:
The company's numbers: the main line first, then shared lines, then
direct lines (each by label).

users.description:
The company's users who may use Granite Phone (employees, admins),
by name: who numbers can be given to.

AdminQuestion.description: A question, for the admin page.

AgentResult.description:
The agent's structured result (`.github/posthog-autofix/result.schema.json`).
It is the agent's claim; [`RunReport::verification`] is what the workflow
proved.

oneOf.description: The repository it changed, if any.

summary.description:
One short sentence: what goes wrong and on which route (the title when
there is no `pr_title`, and the Issue line of an older report).

given.description:
The bug report's Given: the state the bug needs, e.g. `a company with
calling turned off`. Empty from a workflow older than these fields.

when.description: When: the user's action, with the page and the API route.

then.description:
Then: what the system does at that point, e.g. `the API answers 403
calling_disabled`.

impact.description: What users notice, in one sentence; the email adds the counts.

check.description: How a developer sees the fix by hand, in one line; empty without a fix.

root_cause.description: Why it happened, in a few sentences.

fix_summary.description:
One or two short sentences: what the fix changes, naming the function
and file (the Fix line); empty without a fix.

risk.description: What the fix could break, and how likely.

test.description: The test, or why there is none.

recommendation.description: The next step for a person (a suppression rule, a migration to apply).

duplicate_of.description: The pull request or commit that already covers the issue.

AgentToken.description: A token the agent reads the API with.

expires_at.description:
When it stops working (unix seconds); it also stops once the question
is `done` or `failed`.

user_id.description: The asker, whom the token acts as.

company_id.description: The only company the token sees.

partial.description: What the agent answered before failing, if anything.

AgreedTime.description: An agreed estimate time, on the user's clock.

evidence.description: The words that set the time.

on.description: The AI personal assistant (AI promises) runs for me.

AiPromise.description:
A promise the rep made a customer, the quote work a customer gave them,
or something they sent a customer to approve.

kind.description:
`promise`: the rep's; `quote`: the customer's quote to make or update
(one task per customer, what they asked for in `details`); `approval`:
something the rep sent for the customer's approval (due a day later).

crm_action.description:
What the rep does in the CRM that closes the promise by itself:
`contract` (a document sent to sign), `schedule` (an event for the
customer on the schedule) or `call` (a call with them); null when only
a message that keeps it, or Done, closes it. A quote task closes once
one of the customer's quotes is saved or emailed.

customer_id.description: The customer; null for a caller whose number is on no customer.

customer_digits.description: The customer's phone (10 digits), for a call or a text.

customer_email.description: The customer's email, for an email.

customer_label.description:
The name the customer goes by in the call or message (for a caller
whose number is on no customer).

quote_id.description: A quote task's quote: the customer's newest.

title.description: What to do, e.g. "Send the inventory link".

said.description: The words that made it (for a quote task, its latest ask's).

details.description: A quote task's asks, one per line: what the quote must have or change.

is_appointment.description: An appointment at a set time (a visit, measuring, a showroom meeting).

channel.description: `sms` or `email` when a message keeps it.

draft.description: That message, ready to send (null when the AI could not write it).

oneOf.description:
An appointment's event for the customer within 12 hours of it (null:
not on the schedule, or not an appointment).

Another appointment within the hour: one the rep promised someone
else, or an event assigned to them.

waiting.description: Oldest wait first; only without a customer, phone or email.

AnswerAttempt.description: One answer to a training question.

attempt_number.description: Their try at the question, from 1.

selected_answer_id.description: The answer they picked; null when none.

is_correct.description: Whether it was right, as recorded.

question_id.description: Question id (of a questionnaire the caller can use).

answer.description: Answer, up to 10000 characters; empty clears it.

AnsweredQuestion.description: A question with the deal's answer.

answer.description: The deal's answer; empty when not answered.

answers.description: Answers to save; questions the caller cannot use are ignored.

create_note.description: Also add the answered questions to the deal as a note.

note_created.description: A note was added to the deal.

user.description: The signed-in user, in the company requests act in.

user_is_super_admin.description: The user holds the Super Admin position somewhere.

superadmin_companies.description: Companies a super admin can switch to, by name.

active_company_id.description: The company a super admin chose to act in (null when it is their own).

portal.description:
The portal a position locks the user into (`installer`, `check-in`,
`marketing`, `shop_worker`, `template`); null for everyone else.

sections.description:
The sections of the app the user reaches, when a sectioned position
(Inventory Manager, Scheduling Manager) limits them: keys such as
`inventory`, `inventory_admin`, `customers`, `schedule`
(`GET /v1/company/position-sections` lists them all). The API refuses
the rest. Null when they reach the whole app.

has_telnyx_api.description: The company has Granite Phone (Telnyx) switched on.

The company texts through Telnyx (its messaging profile is set):
users with a `telnyx_line` text from it (`/v1/sms/telnyx/...`).

telnyx_line.description:
The user's Telnyx line for calls and texts from the CRM (E.164): their
default caller ID, else their direct number, else the first number
they may call from; null without one (or without Telnyx).

has_inbound_email.description: The company receives email (it has a mail domain).

sms_images_enabled.description: Pictures can be sent by text (`SMS_IMAGES_ENABLED` is not off).

can_manage_company.description: May edit company settings and users (super user, or Manager).

is_shop_manager.description: Holds the Shop Manager position in the company.

is_template_maker.description: Holds Template in the company (their portal is their own schedule).

user_ai_promises.description:
AI promises is on for the user (`users.ai_promises`): the promise list
and the promised messages in the composers.

user_ai_promises_available.description:
The user has the AI personal assistant, on or switched off by them
(the switch on My Account).

feature_capabilities.description: What the user's home company can do, as the guided tours gate on it.

Drawn inside the body (a signature logo) rather than attached; null

signed_url.description: A link the browser can open, for private files (valid an hour).

Whether the user's phones ring now: `available`, `dnd` (Do not

The rep (for a Granite Phone call nobody answered: the owner of the
direct line it rang).

When the call started, as `CloudTalk` reports it (RFC 3339 for a

Direction, outcome, `Recorded`, then `CloudTalk` tags (a Granite Phone

Body of `PUT /v1/phone/call-blocking`: the whole setting (the screen's

What happens to likely spam: `ring` (allow to ring), `block` (the
action for blocked calls) or `voicemail`.

What blocked callers get: `announce` (the announcement, then hang

What blocked callers hear with `announce`, at most 500 characters;

Blocked numbers (any US or Canada format, or E.164) and 3-digit US

transcript_preview.description: The start of the transcript, when one was made.
